summary: Tested Marketplace media extension (photos + videos + background music). Backend: 11/11 pytest cases PASS covering ListingCreate accepting videos[0..5] + audio, defaults to [] and null when absent, 422 on 6 videos, /api/user/uploads accepts .mp3/.m4a/.aac/.ogg/.wav, .txt still returns 415, GET /api/marketplace and GET /api/admin/marketplace both expose media fields, media persists after admin approval. Frontend (Expo Web): 3-section media form renders with correct testids (mkc-add-img/vid/audio + previews with remove and reorder). End-to-end publish flow via UI with 1 photo + 1 video + 1 audio succeeds, navigates to /marketplace where the card shows <video controls>, the floating 'Écouter la musique' pill (data-testid mk-audio-toggle-<id>), the 🎵 badge and photo count. The newly-created listing appears in /api/admin/marketplace with images/videos/audio populated. Feature flags marketplace + marketplace_publish were turned ON before tests and turned OFF after per policy.

integration_issues.issue: When clicking the 'Écouter la musique' pill with a synthetic (invalid) mp3, the label did not switch to 'Musique on'. Could not verify with a real audio file in this run. Suspected: fine in real usage (state flips synchronously before .play() promise), but worth a manual smoke with a real .mp3. No error surfaced in console.

action_items: OPTIONAL: manually verify audio pill actually toggles between 'Écouter la musique' ↔ 'Musique on' with a valid mp3 asset (not blocker).
REMINDER: /api/admin/feature-flags GET/PUT auth vulnerability from iteration_22 was NOT re-verified in this run — carry forward for a future auth-focused pass.
critical_code_review_comments: marketplace.py: `_serialize()` correctly forwards videos and audio because it's a generic {k:v for k,v} on the whole doc — no risk of dropping new fields.

ads.py ALLOWED_UPLOAD is now the union of image+video+audio sets — same endpoint is used for ads uploads too, meaning an ad-only user could upload audio though the ad model doesn't consume it. Low priority (no harm), but consider a per-endpoint whitelist if strict content policing is needed.

marketplace.tsx audio playback relies on Platform.OS==='web' only — native (iOS/Android) users won't hear the background music. Task description explicitly says 'Video/audio playback is web-only via raw <video>/<audio> HTML tags', so this is intentional.
